races.name: Sheahan's Pharmacy 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Flat form shows a win at 8f on standard going and a 5th over 10f on good; a genuine hold-up type running out of his natural position here, and with no hurdles form, his chance in any scenario depends on jumping cleanly in a busy midfield.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Finished 12th of 16 on good ground over 16f last time out, carries a 'fades in finish' flag, and is trained by Hanlon who has had no winners from 20 recent runners; a hold-up type displaced into midfield, with limited evidence of the finishing kick needed.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh in the plate for Harrington is a significant booking in a maiden; ran 4th and 13th in Irish Points on good ground, showing some promise, and a prominent style suits if Sea Of Dubka's pace is catchable from the last.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: A flagged fader whose recent form reads P9U in four starts on good — pulled up, unseated, and a remote 9th — with no wins or places; his true hold-up role will see him running from midfield, and the fade flag is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Has beaten only one horse home across eight starts on good, but carries headgear (blinkers) and ran 6th over 17f hurdles recently; his natural hold-up style will see him running from midfield in a compressed field, and the blinkers add an unknown element.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the mount for Gordon Elliott, a combination worth noting; won on good ground over 10f on the Flat and has placed in two hurdle starts, suggesting a horse who handles this trip and going with a clear racing pattern from a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Manntari
runners_data.note: Just the one run on record — 7th over 12f on good — and ridden by a claiming jockey for McNamara, who has no recent winners; extreme lack of form data makes assessment speculative, and his hold-up profile sees him at the back of a crowded rear group.

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: A horse with back-to-back runner-up finishes over 16-17f on good ground — the most consistent form in the race — and wears a hood; a genuine hold-up operator who will find the midfield area crowded but his proven stamina over this trip range makes him dangerous if a run appears in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second runner, running 7lbs lower in the handicap weights here; career form shows finishes of 10th, 4th, 7th, 11th, 11th on good ground over middle distances, and with no hurdles wins, this is a hold-up type whose best flat-racing effort was modest.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has one win to his name (flat/good), finishing 5th over 17f hurdles last time; Cromwell has five winners in the last fortnight and this horse's prominent style means he should be positioned to attack from two out if jumping is fluent.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Dubka
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good ground under Darragh O'Keeffe for De Bromhead and is the lone natural front-runner here; 34 days off is straightforward, and an uncontested lead on going she handles is a major tactical plus.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Dubka is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner maiden hurdle at Killarney and, with no other natural leader to press her, she is set to dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front on good ground over 2m1f. Chairmanforlife, Harmani, and Misty Cove are the prominent types who will look to sit close to the pace in the slipstream, while the bulk of the field — Divelment, Connor Of Mali, Camp Verde, Another Day Done, Minella Buoy, Manntari, and Guildhall Graduate — are hold-up horses mapped into midfield because the rear of this field is more crowded than the map can represent. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back, meaning several of those horses — most likely Minella Buoy and Divelment, who carry some form — will be shuffled closer to midfield than their natural instincts demand. With Sea Of Dubka able to roll along unchallenged at a sensible gallop, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid-pace racers who travel comfortably in behind and have the finishing resolution to pick her off from two out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Of Dubka Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Dubka sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the prominent trio cannot sustain their challenge from the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Dubka rolls along at a controlled pace, her rivals expending energy trying to close rather than coasting in a rhythm, and the front-runner's fresh-air advantage proves decisive on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string the field out and one of the prominent trio tracks perfectly to lead approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Harmani, with a Flat win on good ground and proven jumping form, or Chairmanforlife under Mark Walsh, tracks the front-runner in a prime position and produces a clean jump at the last to lead; a horse that has been travelling within itself in second or third reaps the reward of a well-judged pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a horse shuffled into midfield finds a gap between tiring rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up horses compressed into the middle of the field, one — most likely Minella Buoy, who has finished second twice over longer trips on good ground — could benefit if the front two or three meet and tire each other out from the last; however, the redistribution of so many natural hold-up types into midfield means traffic risks are high and clear runs scarce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Fragments, Outsider Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses, there is interference among the midfield pack, and a lightly-raced or unexposed horse benefits from chaos.
scenarios.body: Guildhall Graduate or Manntari, both with limited hurdles form, could profit from a messy finish if falls or mistakes disorder the pack; the very low probability reflects the absence of any evidence these horses can produce a winning performance at this level.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Dubka — if she gets a clean round of jumping and is not headed before the last, a front-running performance in an uncontested lead is the single most likely winning scenario in this race.

Minella Buoy — with 22s on good ground over the relevant distances, he is the most consistent horse in the field on form, but watch whether Daniel King can find daylight through the compressed midfield hold-up pack late on.

Harmani and Chairmanforlife — both prominent types with live claims under top jockeys (Kennedy, Walsh); if either gets a perfect pitch just off Sea Of Dubka's shoulder, they represent the main danger to the front-runner.

Connor Of Mali and Camp Verde — both carry 'fades in finish' flags and have poor recent form; their presence compressed into midfield increases the risk of interference for genuine closers like Minella Buoy trying to thread through late.

Misty Cove's tongue-tie — first-time or retained headgear in a Cromwell yard in form (5/16 last 14 days) can be a subtle market mover; watch for any market move that suggests the yard is confident the piece of gear has found the horse's rhythm.

races.name: GMIB Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Jack Kennedy and Cian Collins, suited by Good ground with two course-relevant wins and places at sim going (10/15); at OR=131 he is the highest-rated runner but a poor last-time-out finishing position (8th) over further suggests he needs things to fall right from the back.|

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer in career-best form (placed last time at OR=126 on Good), Daniel King takes over; sharp enough to press Hi Ho Idaho from an early stage and Good going suits (12/15 sim-going record) — the 2m1f trip is comfortably within his range.|

runners_data.name: Feud
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Sean Flanagan returning after a 214-day break with a troubled recent form string (P090F); two course-sim wins suggest ability on Good ground but the lengthy absence and jumping errors are significant risk flags that make this a difficult proposition.|

runners_data.name: Hi Ho Idaho
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field; Danny Gilligan can dictate unopposed on Good ground over his proven 2m1f trip, and his last-start win completing a consistent 3-3-3-2-1 sequence shows he is in the form of his life — jumping fluency will be key.|

runners_data.name: Black Bamboo
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist returning after 214 days, carrying top weight at 152lbs; sim-going record is ordinary (8/15, no wins) and his recent finishing positions (9-17-13-4-10) show only one decent placing in the past five, making him a difficult each-way proposition.|

runners_data.name: Gino Bella
runners_data.note: In cracking form having won his last two starts over this exact 2m1f trip on Good ground (Killarney-type track), Patrick Foley's six-year-old wears hood and tongue-tie; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps at OR=115 and the sim-going record (8/14) is acceptable — prominent racer ideally positioned.|

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim is an asset for Eoin McCarthy's charge, but this eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up racer — placed into the midfield map only because the rear of the field is congested; his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 underlines that racing out of natural position tempers his chance, even on his favoured Good turf (14/15 sim-going).|

runners_data.name: Moylussa
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe partners this consistent placer for Maike Magnussen — two recent thirds show solid handicap form, but Moylussa's instinct is to come from the back, and with the rear already crowded, getting a clean run from off the pace over 2m1f is a genuine obstacle; STYLE_FIT 0.91 reflects the compromised positioning.|

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright takes the mount on Stuart Curling's six-year-old, who has finished between sixth and eighth in every one of his last five — the pattern of consistency without winning is a concern; wears headgear (tongue-tie and hood) and, like several others, is a genuine closer mapped out of his natural rear position because of the hold-up crowd.|

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Donal Commins with back-to-back second-place finishes at sim going, showing she can get competitive at OR=104; however, she is a true closer wearing tongue-tie and hood, and as one of four redistributed hold-up types she faces a positioning challenge — the 17-day turnaround is fine, but her chance depends on getting daylight at the business end.|

races.paceDynamic: Hi Ho Idaho is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Danny Gilligan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over this 2m1f trip on Good ground. The pace will be honest but unforced — Hi Ho Idaho's recent win at OR=120 came making all, and nothing in this field has either the natural inclination or the positional speed to seriously contest the front rank. Autumn Twist and Gino Bella will push into prominent positions just behind, creating a small lead group from which the race will be run, while the bulk of the field — Fiveonefive, Feud, Black Bamboo, Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench, and Eye Contact — will be held up or tracking midfield. Crucially, Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench, and Eye Contact are genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with closers; Autumn Twist and Gino Bella are most likely to actually secure the prominent positions behind Hi Ho Idaho. This race shape — a single unchallenged leader setting a measured pace — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and produce a sustained run from two out, giving the lead-to-prominent profile a significant structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Idaho Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho gets a soft lead unchallenged and the prominent pair press from two out in a straightforward stamina test.
scenarios.body: Hi Ho Idaho controls tempo throughout, with Autumn Twist and Gino Bella travelling just off the pace and producing their runs at the second-last; the measured gallop suits horses who can quicken off a sound but not brutal pace. Prominent racers with Good-ground form get first run on the hold-up brigade who will be threading through from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Burst From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho's controlled pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up horses get a dream run through from two out.
scenarios.body: A steady early gallop compresses the field, leaving the closers poised but the race not truly run at a searching enough tempo to fully expose a free-running leader; Fiveonefive or Feud could benefit if they get a clear passage. However, several of the nominal closers (Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench, Eye Contact) are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to get ideal positioning, which tempers this scenario's probability markedly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho finds extra reserves in the final flight and none of the prominent challengers can match his jumping fluency.
scenarios.body: With a clear lead and a sound jumper in form — his last three runs all placed or winning — Hi Ho Idaho simply outstays the field in a grinding finish up the Killarney straight. Gino Bella, who is in excellent recent form with back-to-back wins, would be the biggest danger if Idaho weakens, but a fluent round of jumping under a confident Gilligan makes this a live outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Implodes, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pack is bunched entering the home straight and traffic trouble eliminates the hold-up types from contention.
scenarios.body: With so many closers jostling for position on the Killarney track — which can bottleneck — the redistributed hold-up horses (Fast Felix, Lord Ffrench, Eye Contact) face the greatest risk of finding no daylight. Feud's lengthy 214-day absence and Lord Ffrench's consistent mid-pack finishes would be further compounded by a muddling affair that ultimately plays into Hi Ho Idaho's or Autumn Twist's hands anyway.

watchPoints.text: Hi Ho Idaho's unchallenged lead is the race's structural pivot — if Danny Gilligan finds any gaps in the early exchanges or Hi Ho Idaho jumps poorly at any hurdle, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race opens up for the prominent pair.

Autumn Twist and Gino Bella will both look to press Hi Ho Idaho from an early stage — if both push up simultaneously the lead group could be three abreast, injecting more pace than expected and potentially benefiting the back-markers.

Feud's 214-day absence is a significant flag under Sean Flanagan — watch the pre-race market moves closely, as any greenness or jumping errors after such a long break could cause interference in a tightly grouped midfield.

With Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench, and Eye Contact all genuinely wanting to come from the rear but mapped into midfield, watch for a bunched home turn — Killarney's track configuration can create severe traffic problems for closers who are already compromised in positioning.

Black Bamboo carries the burden of a 214-day absence alongside a 152lb top weight at age nine — monitor his jumping sharpness early; if he flukes a clear passage it is worth noting, but his profile suggests he is more a market informer than a serious player here.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Loch Cuan
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's prominent-style operator arrives on the back of two wins on Good ground at 22f, making the step to 2m7f a sensible ask; form reads 02-211 with a solid recent rhythm and James Smith claims 5lbs, and the consistent sim-going record (2W3P) flags him as a genuine contender from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Brother Walfrid
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here for Elliott and Jack Kennedy — tongue-tied, won over 19f on Good and has solid front-running form; 21 days since his last run is fine and he faces no rivals likely to dispute the lead, meaning he can dictate fully and conserve energy for the long 2m7f trip.

runners_data.name: Don Jefe
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by nature, though shown in midfield on the map because the field is stacked with closers; 137 days off the track is a significant question mark, and his best form (1/20f on Yielding to Soft) came on softer ground than today's Good, so the style constraint and fitness angle both temper his appeal here.

runners_data.name: Local News
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two hurdle starts (1/24f and 1/19f, both Good), this six-year-old for Richard Hennessy is a genuine hold-up type who will need things to develop in his favour from off the pace; 81 days since his last run is modest, but his clean 2W2P on similar going is the strongest sim-going profile in the field and a late-rolling race could unlock him.

runners_data.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 131 and trained by Mullins with Brian Hayes aboard, but his Good-ground sim-going record is an uncomfortable 0 wins from 3 comparable starts; tongue-tied and coming off a third-place run 35 days ago, he will need to sweep from the rear in a race where the front-runner is uncontested and the prominent horses are well-placed.

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount on this prominent-style mare who has strong recent form — two wins and a second from her last four completed starts including at 24f and 23f on Good; only 12 days since her last run suggests freshness is not a concern, and her style suits this race shape perfectly as a prominent tracker behind Brother Walfrid.

races.paceDynamic: Brother Walfrid is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Jack Kennedy in the plate for Gordon Elliott, he will stride into the lead from the off over this 2m7f trip on Good ground. The three hold-up horses — Local News, Diamond Du Berlais, and Don Jefe — will be forced to track further back than ideal, creating a clean, unchallenged lead for Brother Walfrid who can dictate his own rhythm without pressure. Loch Cuan and Pets Georgina will slot in prominently just behind the leader, giving this race a well-strung-out, single-file quality with a sustainable gallop rather than a frenetic one. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically position themselves at the rear in an orthodox sense — Don Jefe has been redistributed to midfield on the map, but the true hold-up runners (Local News, Diamond Du Berlais) will need to deliver significant late runs from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can travel in behind Brother Walfrid and pick him off in the straight, making Loch Cuan and Pets Georgina the profiles best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brother Walfrid Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Brother Walfrid establishes an uncontested lead and the prominent horses cannot sustain their challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Brother Walfrid dictates a measured pace under Jack Kennedy, jumping cleanly throughout the 2m7f trip, and the hold-up horses face too much ground to make up on the run-in; the prominent runners close but the leader has enough in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Brother Walfrid's lead proves just beyond sustainable and one of the prominent trackers delivers a clean jumping round to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Loch Cuan or Pets Georgina, tracking the leader in second or third, moves smoothly to challenge from the second-last and uses the Good ground to assert on the run to the line; their recent winning form on similar going makes them suited to this resolution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning in and Brother Walfrid ties up, creating a sprint for home that suits closers.
scenarios.body: Local News, with two wins from two hurdle starts on Good ground and a 6-week freshener, would be the most dangerous beneficiary, finishing strongly with a clear run; Diamond Du Berlais carries the highest OR at 131 but his disappointing Good-ground record (0 wins from 3 similar runs) tempers confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there is a significant incident at a hurdle, a fall or unseating that reshuffles the field entirely.
scenarios.body: With 12 hurdles to jump over 2m7f on Good ground, any mishap from one of the less-fluent jumpers could create a stop-start pace and benefit whoever survives with a clear run; Diamond Du Berlais and Don Jefe, both lightly raced over hurdles in varying conditions, carry the most uncertainty.

watchPoints.text: Brother Walfrid holds a clean lead — watch whether Jack Kennedy elects to quicken from the third-last or conserve; if he idles, Loch Cuan and Pets Georgina are positioned to pounce immediately.

Don Jefe's 137-day absence combined with his redistribution out of his natural hold-up role means he faces dual headwinds — watch his jumping and early positioning to assess whether he settles without incident.

Local News is unbeaten in two but steps into deeper handicap company with a 3lb claimer aboard; watch whether Josh Williamson (3) can hold him up cleanly without losing too much ground in a string-out field.

Diamond Du Berlais, despite his lofty OR of 131, has a telling 0W from 3 on Good going in similar-distance events — watch whether Brian Hayes attempts to ride him handier than usual to compensate for the hold-up deficit in this race shape.

The 2m7f trip at Killarney involves 12 hurdles and a long run-in — watch the jumping fluency of Brother Walfrid in the early stages, as any mistake at a fence on the first circuit could compress the field and change the pace entirely.

races.name: Thorn Plant Hire Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Ballystone
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on soft and placed on good going, this eight-year-old is a natural hold-up performer that the race shape pushes forward into midfield — its chance depends heavily on the pace burning out ahead of it, which is not guaranteed with two genuine front-runners present.

runners_data.name: Fort Dino
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old won on heavy and has shown promise in limited starts; 112 days off the track is a concern but prominent racing style suits a race run at a genuine clip, and Darragh O'Keeffe is a key booking.

runners_data.name: Happy Me
runners_data.note: Poor recent form string (0-6P58) does not encourage, and while a natural hold-up type, it is squeezed into a midfield position by the race shape — the combination of out-of-role running and modest recent figures makes this a tough assignment at OR=120.

runners_data.name: Heroes Rise
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has a solid placed record (2-4-3-2 from recent starts on good ground) but has not run in 508 days; if fitness is there, it is the most naturally talented of the hold-up horses and the form profile suggests it handles this trip and going well.

runners_data.name: Lemmy Caution
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner with a win and multiple places on good ground, this Elliott five-year-old will press for the lead from flag-fall and sets the race up for others if it finds this trip stretching stamina over the final half-mile.

runners_data.name: Themanintheanorak
runners_data.note: Has finished sixth in five of its last six outings, which is hard to ignore; prominent racing style gives it an ideal tactical position in this shape, but the repetitive finishing position suggests it struggles to find the necessary change of gear when it matters.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Mullins' seven-year-old holds an OR=122 lead in the weights but recent form reads 60P-00 and similar-going figures show it finishing well down the field; hard to make a case despite the yard's 11/26 T14 record, and true hold-up style is compromised by the race shape.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR=124 and the lightest weight at 159lbs, Cian Collins' six-year-old has a consistent form string of /10-22 and won on good going over a similar trip; as a confirmed front-runner, it will dictate terms but must hold on if Lemmy Caution pushes it into a hard early duel.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m7½f trip at Killarney, creating a genuine, honest gallop on good ground — neither looks the type to surrender without a fight, so an early duel is the most likely shape. With two horses committed to the front and a field of eight over a staying trip, the pace will be set early and maintained, suiting horses that can travel close to it rather than those forced to make up ground from far back. Prominent racers like Fort Dino and Themanintheanorak are best placed to exploit the honest tempo, sitting just off the leaders and pouncing if either pace-setter ties up. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Ballystone and Happy Me are genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield because Heroes Rise and Where's My Jet also need to come from off the pace — in a race this honest, hold-up types face a stern test of their finishing speed, and the race shape clearly favours horses that can race prominently and stay the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution fight for supremacy throughout, setting a true pace that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will see one or both pace-setters weaken in the final half-mile, leaving Fort Dino or Themanintheanorak — travelling just off the speed — to pick up the pieces with stamina intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lead pair establishes a clear advantage early and the other drops away, allowing controlled front-running.
scenarios.body: A lone leader sets a sustainable rhythm over the staying trip and proves too difficult to peg back on good ground; Affinity Rock's OR=124 and stronger recent form make it the likelier beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Into It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns itself out severely enough that genuine stayers tracking from midfield can deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Heroes Rise, returning after a 508-day absence but with strong placed form on similar going, would be the primary beneficiary if fresher legs tell in the closing stages; Ballystone, though redistributed from its natural hold-up role, has a course win at a similar level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dawdle Turns Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner is willing to commit fully, producing an uncharacteristically slow early pace that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over this trip becomes a stamina-neutral test decided by a late sprint, favouring horses with tactical speed; Fort Dino and Heroes Rise carry enough class to cope, while Happy Me's redistributed midfield position still leaves it chasing from further than ideal.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first three fences to see which horse submits; whoever capitulates first may have had its race ruined, and whoever leads risks burning out.

Fort Dino has not run in 112 days and this is only its third career start — a prominent racing style suits the shape, but race fitness after a long absence over a staying trip of 2m7½f is a legitimate concern worth monitoring in the market.

Heroes Rise returns after a 508-day layoff for Gordon Elliott — despite strong form before the break, a horse absent for that long tackling a 2m7½f steeplechase needs to be treated with significant caution regardless of its ability on paper.

Themanintheanorak has posted six or worse in five of its last six runs — if it repeats that pattern from a prominent position, it is a useful race-shape barometer showing that the gallop is genuine and the distance is testing all runners.

Where's My Jet (Mullins, T14: 11/26) holds market significance despite poor recent form — any significant downward move in betting should be respected given the trainer's current strike rate, even if the form book alone does not encourage.

races.name: Easyfix Equine Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a recent win over 20f on Good (12 days ago), in-form with blinkers applied; likely to race in the rear third and depend on a strong pace that this shape may not provide, so check if the race truly develops.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with consistent form over Good but zero wins from 15 similar-going runs; tongue-tie fitted, jockey claim helps the weight, but a steady pace in this shape makes his task significantly harder from the rear.

runners_data.name: King Ferdinand
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who shapes as the lone pace-setter here; the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects that he's rated below his rivals, but his ability to control tempo uncontested at 2m7½f on Good ground is the central tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Kilkee Bay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who won over 22f on Soft and placed on Good; races from hold-up to midfield and has blinkers on, with course form worth noting — capable of outrunning his odds if the race develops into a jumping test.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good (45 days ago), solid stamina credentials at this trip; Donagh Meyler rides and his recent win is an obvious form reference, though 45 days between runs needs monitoring and he'll need to find a better position than his natural hold-up style affords here.

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type who has placed at 26f on Good; Phillip Enright is a strong booking, and with only King Ferdinand ahead of him, Je Suis is ideally drawn in terms of race shape to track the leader and apply pressure from the second-last.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with two recent wins including a 23f success on Good; Darragh O'Keeffe is an excellent tactical jockey who may navigate a better position than the redistribution suggests, but the compressed pace shape limits the advantage this young mare's finishing kick would normally extract.

runners_data.name: Walk Away Harry
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the finish alongside a 80-day absence, and his natural style is hold-up — pushed into midfield on the map only because the field is overloaded with rear-runners; the combination of fitness question, style mismatch and slow pace makes him a difficult proposition here.

runners_data.name: Wakey Wakey Man
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with an encouraging second over 20f on Soft; true hold-up type nudged forward on the map rather than a genuine front-runner, carrying a 99-day absence — the fitness concern is real and the race shape doesn't aid his style in any case.

runners_data.name: Mount Shenshan
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride on this hold-up type whose recent form shows nothing worse than a three (hist includes 3/26f/GOO); races from deep and a slow pace from King Ferdinand means his strong mid-race jumper's profile may not be enough over the final fences without a true gallop to aim at.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with tongue-tie and blinkers; trainer McCarthy has two runners in 14 days which is positive activity, and there's a second over 19f on Good in recent form — but a 34-day break, natural hold-up style, and the one-paced race shape all work against him.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Prominent-running eight-year-old who won over 23f on Good and has several placed efforts at this track and trip; Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim is a bonus and, with blinkers on, he is likely to settle just behind King Ferdinand — a genuinely well-placed runner for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with tongue-tie and blinkers; has placed at 24f on Good and trainer McLoughlin has a runner 14 days ago showing yard activity, but his natural rear-running style is poorly suited to a slow-pace scenario and his redistribution to midfield overstates his likely tactical position.

races.paceDynamic: King Ferdinand is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no other genuine pace-setter to pressure him, he is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m7½f of Good ground at Killarney. Je Suis and Cullenwaine are the only other prominent types, meaning King Ferdinand can lead with minimal early contest and regulate tempo entirely to his own liking. At a distance this far, an uncontested lead at a steady pace over Good turf is dangerous — it flatters the front-runner and compresses the race into a late stamina test rather than an honest gallop that would bring hold-up horses into play. This race shape strongly favours King Ferdinand and those able to travel prominently in his slipstream (Je Suis, Cullenwaine), as a falsely slow early pace will leave deep closers with insufficient ground to make up. Several runners listed as midfield — including Ladies Well, Walk Away Harry, Wakey Wakey Man, Mount Shenshan, Tropical Image and Malton Groove — are true hold-up types redistributed forward on the map because the field contains far more rear-rankers than the pace shape can accommodate at the back; of those, Ladies Well and Western Model are most capable of actually securing a useful tracking position, with the rest condemned to race wide or deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Ferdinand Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand is allowed to set a slow-to-moderate tempo unchallenged and the race becomes a stamina test from the home turn.
scenarios.body: King Ferdinand leads throughout at a controlled pace, and the lack of genuine pressing means closers have no honest gallop to close into; those tracking closest — Je Suis and Cullenwaine — get the perfect position to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that King Ferdinand fades in the final mile but prominent/prominent-tracking horses are ideally poised to strike.
scenarios.body: Je Suis or Cullenwaine race prominently throughout and hit the front at the second-last, while deeper hold-up types fail to get competitive as the race doesn't truly fall apart at the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land a Blow
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns himself and the prominent horses off, creating a truly run race that suits closers.
scenarios.body: A sustained pace stretches the field and allows a hold-up horse with stamina — Ladies Well or Western Model — to emerge from the pack with a sustained run from the final fence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Race Shape
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand jumps poorly or is taken on early, causing an erratic tempo with scrambling for position in a large field.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners over fences on Good ground, falls, mistakes or a sudden pace collapse could randomise the result, allowing an each-way type with course form to emerge; Kilkee Bay and Oneforgonzo are best-placed to capitalise on a disrupted race.

watchPoints.text: King Ferdinand's jumping — if he makes an early error at one of the first few fences in a 13-runner field, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race could fall to a hold-up type rather than the prominent runners who benefit from his controlled lead.

Ladies Well and Western Model may attempt to push forward early to overcome their natural hold-up styles; if they succeed in tracking closer than expected, their form gives them a live chance, but watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe or Donagh Meyler actually commit to a more forward position at the start.

Walk Away Harry's fade flag combined with an 80-day absence makes him a notable risk in a 13-runner field over fences — he could interfere with other runners if he weakens dramatically in the final mile.

Wakey Wakey Man and Mount Shenshan both carry 99-day and 23-day absences respectively; watch the market for significant moves that would suggest stable confidence in their fitness, as either could outrun their odds if fresh and travelling well.

With seven hold-up types redistributed in the field, early positioning at the first fence will be critical — watch for crowding or bumping as genuine rear-runners attempt to find their natural spot, which could compromise several runners' chances before the race properly develops.

races.name: Brehon Hotel & Spa Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Illtakehimmyself
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid recent form (wins and places on Good), ridden by claimer Calum Hogan (5lb); 35 days off is untroubling, course trip suits, but must be produced from off the pace in a race that may not generate enough late gallop to reel in front players.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who showed a close second last time over this sort of trip on Good; fresh off a 12-day turnaround which is quick for a chaser, and the pace scenario may not produce the gap he needs from behind.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Des Chastys
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist with fine Good-ground form, two wins over this course distance profile; 203 days absent is a significant stamina question-mark even if McNamara keeps his horses fit, but jumping experience could prove vital if the race falls apart.

runners_data.name: Ollie La Ba Ba
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner — this is his role and he has the licence to dictate today; trainer McCarthy is 2/6 in the last 14 days showing current yard form, but his record suggests he finds his optimum only when allowed to bowl along, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he rarely wins from this position when actually tested.

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing eight-year-old who ran just seven days ago — the quick turnaround is a clear watch point on fitness and freshness; strong Good-ground record (all 15 runs), which is a meaningful positive, and his natural prominent style suits a race with only one leader.

runners_data.name: Tippin And Tappin
runners_data.note: Dual course winner over Good ground, genuinely progressive in 2023-24; natural hold-up type whose two wins came when able to get cover and pick up late, but this pace map has him mapped forward of where he'll likely race — his chance hinges on whether the tempo is truly strong enough to bring him into it.

runners_data.name: Toon Town
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a genuine Good-ground win on his CV but whose true style is hold-up despite the midfield map position; short 17-day turnaround noted, and at this class level his tendency to race without cover means he'll need a clear passage in a tightly-grouped field.

runners_data.name: Seeitoldya
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old whose recent form is modest (falls, pulled up, mid-field finishes); a natural closer pushed further back than ideal in this field configuration, and the Hanlon yard is 0/20 over the past 14 days — a significant cold-stable flag.

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field congestion; best form came over shorter trips (16f wins), and stepping to 2m5f on a galloping Good track at Killarney is a clear stamina test this profile may not be equipped to pass.

runners_data.name: Miners Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a consistent placed record on Good ground and strong course-distance profile; Enright is a shrewd booking, and a 17-day turnaround looks fine — this horse is likely to fill the role of lead-tracker behind Ollie La Ba Ba and is a key player if the front holds on.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old at the bottom of the handicap (OR 82) with a string of mid-field and rear finishes on Good; a genuine deep hold-up type further back than the map shows, and zero wins or placed efforts from the last five runs on this surface offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Ollie La Ba Ba is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner handicap chase over 2m5f on Good ground at Killarney, and with no other natural leader to push him, he is set to control the pace from the front without serious early pressure. Burru and Miners Bridge are the most likely to race prominently behind him, giving the race a defined shape: leader on a sensible gallop, a small group tracking, and a cluttered hold-up pack behind. This field is loaded with genuine hold-up types — Toon Town, Tippin And Tappin, Shannon Bank, Seeitoldya, and Ferdia all sit naturally at the rear but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate that many closers at the back; in practice, several of these will be further back than shown and will face a stiffer challenge to get competitive. On Good ground over a trip that rewards relentless galloping rather than a sprint finish, the sustainable gallop set by Ollie La Ba Ba at Killarney — a course where the run-in is unforgiving — sets up best for horses who travel prominently or can make smooth headway from midfield with a genuine ground-eating stride, not horses forced to launch from deep off a moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ollie Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Ollie La Ba Ba is allowed to roll along at his own rhythm and no rival applies meaningful pressure before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Ollie La Ba Ba controls tempo on a fair gallop, the hold-up horses are too far back to mount a telling challenge, and the prominent/midfield travellers who can sustain the pace fare best up the Killarney straight; Good ground and an uncontested lead rewards those who are already travelling on the bridle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Burru or Miners Bridge move into serious contention from the third-last fence, forcing a contested finish between prominent types.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a stamina contest between horses that have raced handily throughout, and hold-up types making late runs are left with too much ground to make up over the final two fences; Good ground amplifies the advantage of horses who have saved energy by tracking rather than chasing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to bring the best hold-up runners into play off the home turn with a clear run.
scenarios.body: A true closer such as Illtakehimmyself or Kings Jet, placed handily enough in practice despite their natural style, produces a sustained late run if the prominent horses crack; however this scenario is structurally discounted because the redistributed hold-up horses are unlikely to secure their ideal deep position and may be crowded wide.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a collapse in the pace causes carnage through the field, presenting a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up types scrambling for position and fences to negotiate, a messy race could produce an unexpected winner from midfield if the front group makes costly errors; Gaelic Des Chastys, a seasoned ten-year-old with Good-ground form, could capitalise given experienced jumping.

watchPoints.text: Burru ran just seven days ago — monitor market moves and any pre-race reports on his freshness, as the quick turnaround in a stamina test could tell against him if he didn't fully recover.

Ollie La Ba Ba controls the race tempo entirely; if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, his STYLE_FIT discount becomes less relevant and he becomes a live danger — watch him closely in the early stages to assess whether he's truly dictating or just drifting.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Toon Town, Tippin And Tappin, Shannon Bank, Seeitoldya, Ferdia) will create congestion at the rear early — watch the first two fences for scrimmaging and potential early jumping errors in a tightly-packed rear group.
Gaelic Des Chastys returns from 203 days off — the market will signal whether McNamara has him ready; if backed, respect the fitness angle, but treat a weak market move as a strong flag to oppose.

Seeitoldya's trainer John Joseph Hanlon is 0/20 in the last 14 days — a notably cold spell for a yard that often relies on strike-rate patterns; factor this into any assessment of runners from this stable.

races.name: Gallivan Financial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Crowsatedappletart
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with two wins at similar trips on good ground, the 5lb claimer Kenneally reduces the 166lb burden; tongue-tie and cheekpieces in place, just 17 days between runs, and consistent course form makes this a live each-way participant travelling near the pace.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Two wins from her last three completed starts, including a win on good ground over the trip, and her trainer has placed one runner from twelve in the last fortnight — she is in fine form and her prominent style is perfectly suited to a race Costacurta sets up at a manageable tempo.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with an excellent strike rate on good ground (14 from 15 runs on similar surfaces) but a form string that rarely converts — the tongue-tie is noted, Sexton takes off 7lb, and the drop back to 2m1f may sharpen his jumping rhythm even if his finishing kick has disappointed.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who will get a clean lead under O'Keeffe for De Bromhead, whose yard has been in excellent form (4 from 38 in the last fortnight); goes on good ground reliably (7 from 8 runs) and the uncontested lead over a flat, right-handed Killarney circuit is a significant structural advantage.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best recent effort was a second over 16f on good ground; the 5lb apprentice O'Sullivan is a useful booking but this horse has registered three non-completions and three poor finishes in recent starts, so jumping reliability is a concern in a Steeplechase context.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Has posted a series of fifth-place finishes suggesting a horse that gets into contention without finding extra — the hood is noted, Cromwell's yard has fired in five from sixteen recently, but 47 days off and a record of PU and pulled-up runs last time out warrant caution in a chase context.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good ground two starts ago and placed next time out, so he arrives in form; Noonan takes the ride for a stable that has had two winners from six recently, and his prominent style fits naturally into a race where the lead positions are finite and competitive.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has been repositioned to midfield in the pace map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed — his best form shows wins on good ground, but racing closer to the pace than he prefers means his natural finishing effort may arrive too early or not at all, softening his appeal here.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at five, with no wins on record and a form line of 2-5633; a true hold-up type whose tactical position has been squeezed forward by the race shape — the going is fine for him but he is unlikely to get the trailing, patient ride that his limited form suggests he needs.

races.paceDynamic: Costacurta is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe will be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m1f at Killarney. Behind him, Crowsatedappletart and Femme Magnifique are both prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, while Kilbrin Rocco adds a third prominent racer into a field where the front positions will be contested but not violently so. Piccolo Player and Ballybrittas are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is already over-subscribed — they will not get their true trailing position and will race closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers their prospects in a shape that doesn't ask them to come from the clouds. With one horse able to control the tempo cleanly, this race strongly favours horses who can travel prominently at a measured pace and kick off the last fence — the prominent-to-lead profile is the dominant shape to concentrate on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Costacurta Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Costacurta sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays honest rather than crawling, the race becomes a test of jumping and staying power at the business end.
scenarios.body: O'Keeffe dictates on Costacurta from gate to finish over a track and trip he handles well on good ground, with the race unfolding at a rhythm that suits a horse who has placed twice at the trip over similar conditions. Prominent rivals Crowsatedappletart and Femme Magnifique, both with good form on good ground, have the tactical speed to track and pounce, making this scenario the natural home for the two highest-rated prominent horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outguns Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Costacurta's pace is steady enough to be tracked comfortably and a prominent challenger times a well-judged run from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Femme Magnifique or Crowsatedappletart, travelling on the heels of the leader, uses superior recent form or freshness to collar Costacurta on the run-in — Femme Magnifique in particular has won twice at this sort of trip and goes well fresh on good ground. Kilbrin Rocco, having won over 16f on good ground and ridden by the in-form stable combination, is also capable of making a bold show from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Lands Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the straight to string the race out and create a gap for a horse finishing from behind the leaders.
scenarios.body: War Correspondent has the highest volume of good-ground form in this field and, while results have been modest, the step back to 2m1f from further trips could sharpen him up, and Sexton's claim helps at the weights. Beauforts Storm placed here over this trip on good ground and possesses the profile to pick up horses if the race is run at a true gallop — but both depend on a pace scenario that the sole front-runner Costacurta is unlikely to manufacture on his own.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Costacurta weakens sharply, creating late ground for true closers racing out of their natural position.
scenarios.body: Piccolo Player and Ballybrittas are genuine hold-up horses forced closer to the pace than ideal given field composition — their best chance exists only if the race develops into a muddling contest with a strong late surge required. Both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and the structural reality is they are unlikely to get the true waiting ride that suits them, making this the least probable shape.

watchPoints.text: Costacurta's jumping must be monitored at the first fence — if he is slow or makes a mistake early, the uncontested lead he needs to control tempo disappears immediately, fundamentally reshaping the race.

Femme Magnifique and Crowsatedappletart are both prominent types who will want the same ground behind Costacurta — a bumping, competitive duel for position from the first circuit could burn out both, benefiting something off the pace.

Beauforts Storm has a U (unseated) on his recent form card and Stuntman Steve a PU — in a Steeplechase on a testing track, watch for early fallers that could bring down others and change the complexion of the race dramatically.

Ballybrittas and Piccolo Player, both redistributed hold-up types running closer than ideal, could become a traffic hazard in the middle of the field if they find themselves between horses and unable to drop out to their natural position approaching the final circuit.

The going has been reported Good consistently across all eight races today at Killarney — no meaningful deterioration is expected, so runners with consistent good-ground form hold their profile throughout.

races.name: Peadar's Pub Glenbeigh Flat Race

runners_data.name: Con Did It
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old with a completely unknown running style making this a difficult profile to map; Mr J Dunne (7lb claimer) rides for Eoin Christopher McCarthy whose stable has shown recent activity (T14: 2/6), suggesting this runner may be more ready than the bare form implies.

runners_data.name: Stary Notions
runners_data.note: Another unexposed six-year-old with no discernible pace profile from available form, making this a genuine unknown quantity; the P M Lynch yard has had no runners in the past 14 days which offers no warm clue, though at level weights in a flat race any improvement could make this competitive.

runners_data.name: Suresuresure
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator on good ground with a fading tendency in the finish — a worrying combination when the pace is likely to be modest; the form string of 8P-075 shows no wins or places in similar conditions and the 45-day absence adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: The Last Line
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a placed effort (2nd) over 17f on good ground — the most relevant recent form in the field for this trip and going combination; returning after 776 days off which is a significant concern, though John E & Thomas Kiely's runner may have needed time and could be Cherry-ripe now.

runners_data.name: Iron Sword
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a pair of placed efforts in his short career; the four-year-old has raced recently (16 days ago) and his good-ground form figures suggest he handles these conditions, making him a natural fit for a race run at a steady clip from the front.

runners_data.name: Rocky Alfonso
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with one run (4th on soft) whose style is unknown despite the OK going tag; lightly raced with scope for improvement and S Curling's stable (T14: 0/5) has not been firing lately — Mr Derek O'Connor's experience in point-to-point grade could be the difference.

runners_data.name: Walkineezy
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner whose STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) suggests this prominent mapping is somewhat out of natural character, so the pace he sets may not be as fierce as a dedicated front-runner would supply; the Denis Gerard Hogan yard is active and competitive (T14: 2/27) but the shape he creates will largely define this race for everyone else.

runners_data.name: Killeedy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the Willie Mullins powerhouse stable (T14: 11/26), giving this runner strong trainer support in a race where the pace may not be hot enough to set up a late finish; Mr P W Mullins in the saddle adds further confidence, though the single-run form (4th at 17f on good) leaves questions about whether the horse can quicken from off the pace at a steady gallop.

runners_data.name: Streamhill
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with four runs showing 5-5-5-4 finishes on good ground — dependable but seemingly unable to win from behind when the race doesn't truly test stamina; the seven-year-old returns after 66 days and Ms G M Dorgan (7lb claim) may need to adopt a more aggressive ride to overcome the likely modest pace.

races.paceDynamic: Walkineezy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner flat race over 2m1f on good ground at Killarney, and with no rival willing or able to press for the lead, the pace is likely to be measured and controlled from the front. The Prominent types — The Last Line and Iron Sword — will track close behind but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the front and dictate, meaning Walkineezy should find a comfortable rhythm without being harassed. With a sustainable, uncontested gallop anticipated, the race is unlikely to develop into a true test of stamina late on, and hold-up horses such as Killeedy, Streamhill, and Suresuresure will need their jockeys to be proactive and make ground earlier than ideal. This shape strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles only if the pace is genuinely strong enough to set them up — but with one easy-going leader, prominent racers who can travel close to the tempo and quicken from a good position are better placed than deep closers who depend on a hot gallop to be delivered into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Walkineezy Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Walkineezy leads at a steady clip and the prominent trackers The Last Line and Iron Sword travel smoothly in tow before challenging turning for home.
scenarios.body: Walkineezy sets a manageable pace that suits horses who can race close to the tempo and respond when the race quickens in the home straight; with no pressure from behind, the race becomes a positioning exercise and those on the pace have a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the race develops into a true stamina test, enabling the patient hold-up horses to stay on powerfully.
scenarios.body: Killeedy (Willie Mullins stable, likely well-prepped) and Streamhill, who has a consistent profile of staying-on fifth-place finishes, would be the chief beneficiaries of a truly run race where the front end weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Walkineezy, allowed a completely uncontested lead at an easy gallop, simply puts rivals to sleep and wins on the bridle without being tested.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied throughout, Walkineezy could dictate every yard and be too far clear by the home turn for prominent horses to reel in; Denis Gerard Hogan's stable is in fine form (T14: 2/27) and Mr H C Swan is a capable pilot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed or unknown-style runners — Con Did It or Stary Notions — has improved significantly and produces a career-best showing under a shrewd ride.
scenarios.body: Both Con Did It and Stary Notions carry unknown pace profiles and are lightly raced at OR=120, meaning there is genuine scope for one to outrun their market position if either has been quietly prepared for this; at a steady gallop the field remains bunched and a fresh horse could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Walkineezy's actual gallop speed will determine everything — if Mr H C Swan allows a crawl, hold-up horses Killeedy and Streamhill will be caught flat-footed and the race becomes a sprint for those on the pace.
The Last Line returns after 776 days off and any signs of ring rustiness (jumping shadows, hanging, slow into stride) would immediately discount this prominent runner's chance of featuring.

Killeedy represents Willie Mullins (T14: 11/26) whose strike rate demands respect even when the pace shape is not ideal for a hold-up horse — watch for Mr P W Mullins pushing forward earlier than expected to compensate.

Con Did It and Stary Notions are both completely unknown in terms of running style — if either breaks sharply and contests the lead with Walkineezy, the entire pace scenario changes and hold-up horses could get a more genuine gallop to aim at.
Iron Sword raced 16 days ago and is therefore the freshest of the prominent types — recent racecourse sharpness could prove an edge if the contest quickens sharply in the straight.
